subject: Load-test coordination for Acme - concurrency / streaming SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Gomez <luis.gomez@acme.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Load-test coordination for Acme - concurrency / streaming SLOs

Luis — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test on the calendar. Please confirm the details below and share the k6/Locust scripts and a contact for your infra lead.

Summary of SLOs and requirements from today's discovery:
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for text.generate endpoints (50-token responses)
- Throughput: sustained 1,500 RPS for batch scoring endpoint (peak 2,000 RPS during ramp)
- Concurrency: up to 200 concurrent connections for streaming chat sessions (SSE/websocket)
- Streaming: low-latency streaming required for chat UI (token flush <= 150ms)
- Auth: customer will use API keys for test account; we will issue a scoped test key with limited quota

Proposed test plan:
1) Warm-up (10m) — low-rate traffic to warm KV cache and model weights
2) Canary run (30m) — 250 RPS, 25 concurrent streams to validate end-to-end and logging
3) Full ramp (60m) — ramp to 1,500 RPS over 15m, hold 30m, then spike to 2,000 RPS for 15m
4) Post-test: collect traces, p95/p99 latencies, stream jitter, and token throughput

Operational asks for Acme:
- Share k6/Locust scripts (or a Gist) and any custom headers or authentication flow
- Provide public IPs to allowlist (or a CIDR) for the test runners
- Point-of-contact on the test day and preferred test window (we suggested Wed 6/17 10:00-12:30 PT)

Attachments: redwood_test_account_instructions.pdf (test key provisioning + sample curl), acme_loadtest_results_template.csv

If the plan looks good, I will coordinate with Aditya and Dev to provision the test tenant and monitoring. Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the SLOs and the proposed plan look correct from our side. A few notes and attachments:

- Attached is our k6 script (acme_k6_script.js) and a short README describing the custom header auth we use. The k6 script includes the endpoints for text.generate and streaming (using EventSource polyfill).
- We can provide test runners from our CI; will run from two AWS regions (us-west-2 and us-east-1). IPs to allowlist: 3.120.45.0/24 and 18.205.0.0/24.
- Preferred test window: Wed 6/17 10:00-13:00 PT. We can do a dry-run the day before if helpful.
- Internal infra lead: Sarah Chen (sarah.chen@acme.io) — she will be the on-call during the run.

One technical detail: our streaming client opens long-lived connections and sends heartbeat pings every 30s; we saw issues before when proxies close idle connections. Can you confirm keep-alive and max idle timeout on your side? Also curious about your recommended warm-up to populate KV cache and any recommended token bucket settings.

I'll attach the script and README. Let me know if you want the Locust variant instead — we have both.

Thanks,
Luis Gomez
Engineering Manager — Platform
Acme Corp

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Thanks Marissa + Luis — catching up on the thread. A few infra notes from my side: 

1) Capacity: We can support the proposed ramp (2,000 RPS peak) on a dedicated test pool; I'll reserve an instance group and put autoscale buffers in place. I recommend we run the canary against the same pool to validate autoscaling and eviction behavior.

2) Keep-alive / streaming: Our streaming gateway currently has a 5m idle timeout by default; we can extend that to 20m for the test window to ensure long-lived EventSource connections aren't closed. We also support TCP keep-alive; please ensure your client pings match.

3) Allowlist: We'll need the exact CIDRs or IPs your runners will use. Luis's ranges look fine for initial allowlisting (3.120.45.0/24, 18.205.0.0/24). Please confirm any additional egress NAT IPs.

4) Warm-up and KV cache: Strongly recommend a 10–15m warm-up at low QPS to populate prefix/KV caches. Otherwise the first heavy runs will see higher p99 due to cold KV misses. Add a small steady state (100 RPS) pre-warm.

5) Test accounts / keys: Marissa — send me the requested scope for the test API key (rate limits, model pins). We will generate a scoped key and return the credentials via the secure instructions PDF.

6) Monitoring: I'll provision a temporary Grafana dashboard and traces for the run. We should capture per-route token counts, NVMe I/O, and model latency histograms.

If you want, I can join the test-day Slack channel or Zoom for live triage.

— Aditya
